Use `git switch -` to jump back to the previous branch, like `cd -` for git.
`git commit --fixup <sha>` plus `git rebase -i --autosquash` tidies history without manual reordering.
In Python, `functools.cache` memoizes pure functions with one decorator.
Use `python -m http.server` to share a folder over your LAN in seconds.
`git stash push -p` stashes only the hunks you choose.
Prefer `pathlib.Path` over string paths: `Path('a') / 'b'` works on every OS.
`ruff check --fix` and `ruff format` replace flake8, isort and black in one fast tool.
Add `set -euo pipefail` to bash scripts so they fail fast instead of silently continuing.
`git bisect run <test-cmd>` finds the commit that broke something automatically.
Use `dataclass(slots=True)` to cut memory use and catch attribute typos.
Press `Ctrl+R` in your shell to fuzzy-search command history instead of retyping.
`jq -r '.items[] | .name'` extracts fields from JSON on the command line.
Write the failing test first; if it passes immediately, the test is wrong.
`git log -S 'text'` finds the commit that added or removed a string.
Use `enumerate(items, start=1)` instead of manual counters.
In SQL, `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows whether your query uses an index.
`docker system prune` reclaims disk when images and containers pile up.
Use `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` sparingly; swallowed errors hide real bugs.
`curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n' URL` is a quick health probe.
Name boolean variables as questions: `is_ready`, `has_access`.
Use `git worktree add ../fix main` to work on two branches without stashing.
`python -X importtime script.py` shows what slows your startup.
Set timeouts on every network call; the default is often 'wait forever'.
Prefer small pure functions; they are trivially testable and easy to reuse.
`git reflog` can recover commits after a bad reset or rebase.
Use `typing.Protocol` for structural interfaces instead of deep inheritance.
Cache LLM calls by prompt hash to save quota and make reruns deterministic.
`tmux` keeps long-running jobs alive when your SSH session drops.
Keep secrets in environment variables or a secret store, never in the repo.
`sort | uniq -c | sort -nr` is the classic quick frequency count.
